memory_lessons.applicability: For this stencil, compare loop formulations as well as directive choices; the pointer-induction result does not isolate the effect of the SIMD hint.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured no-directive pointer-induction candidate was slower than the row-base-plus-SIMD candidate, but the access forms differ, so the result alone cannot attribute the gap to the directive.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure an indexed row-base loop without a directive against the indexed SIMD candidate under the same correctness and core-budget protocol.

proposal.hypothesis: The measured SIMD candidates (164618338efd47c5 at 0.081288 s and e2786cc8e1da48a4 at 0.082253 s) are close, while the no-directive pointer-induction candidate 2d936b92faa04fe4 measured 0.449431 s and also changed the access form. This experiment uses indexed x accesses through hoisted row bases without a SIMD directive to test whether a compiler-vectorizable loop can approach the explicit-SIMD results. It assumes no alignment or vector width; the ordinary loop covers every valid width and tail. The controller should validate the fixed tolerance and measure both core budgets including setup costs.

retained: Replaced the x pointer-induction loop with an indexed loop over the contiguous x range using the already-hoisted row bases.

Kept the recurrence expression and operation order, boundaries, full initialization, and generic loop bounds; added no SIMD directive, alignment assumption, or fixed-width/tail handling specialization.
